The Metropolitan Police Department (MPD) offers an attractive benefits package. The benefits package includes competitive compensation, health insurance, prescription drug coverage, dental, vision, short- and long-term disability and life insurance, as well a strong retirement benefit and savings options. Employees are also eligible for our employer contributed 401a plan after one year of employment. Additional perks such as discounts on wireless carriers, gym memberships, amusement park tickets and much more! Additional information can be found at: DCHR Benefits

This position is located in the Metropolitan Police Department (MPD), Technical Services Bureau (TSB), Technology Division Chief Information Officer, Customer Support Branch. The mission of MPD is to safeguard the District of Columbia and protect its residents and visitors with the highest regard for the sanctity of human life. We will strive at all times to accomplish our mission with a focus on service, integrity, and fairness by upholding our city’s motto, Justitia Omnibus – Justice for All.

The (TSB) oversees all information technology services, as well as records management, fleet services and evidence control of the IT component of the bureau include software development, data quality and compliance, business application development, and information technology program management. The Records Division provides services like fingerprinting, gun registration, and background checks.

The Program Manager provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, and program management for the Department’s Body-Worn Camera (BWC) and Evidence Retrieval (CCTV) programs. These programs directly support mission-critical public safety operations. The incumbent manages technology systems, personnel, vendor relationships, budgets, compliance requirements, and operational processes to ensure reliability, effectiveness, and continuous improvement. The position serves as a key member of the TSB management team and contributes to organizational strategy, planning, and performance initiatives.

The Incumbent Will Be Responsible For The Following

Serving as a member of the MPD-TSB management team, and in that capacity engages and contributes to the overall performance matrix, strategy, planning, and any other discussion or subject that improves the overall functionality and operational health of the department.
Overseeing and managing the performance efforts related to assigned systems for the MPD BWC and Evidence Retrieval programs; and mapping out project plans from multiple groups. Maintaining support and troubleshoots programs used, including, but not limited to: Axon, Fusus, and drone support.
Leading matrixed teams and cross-functional initiatives to deliver enterprise solutions; providing tactical and strategic leadership for assigned programs; and working with peer organizational leaders in IT, vendors, and client business partners to provide and maintain a robust system solution.
Developing and managing program resource requirements for the Body-Worn Camera (BWC) and digital evidence programs, including budget projections, equipment lifecycle and replacement requirements, software licensing, vendor services, system maintenance, storage capacity, staffing requirements, and planned technology enhancements. Monitoring expenditures and resource utilization; identifying anticipated funding needs and cost risks; and developing recommendations to support annual budget formulation, procurement planning, and long-range program sustainability.
Providing technical and operational recommendations to MPD leadership and appropriate policy officials regarding the technology-related provisions of BWC and digital evidence policies. Evaluating system capabilities, configuration options, operational requirements, data integrity controls, evidence-management practices, and emerging technologies and recommends changes that improve transparency, accountability, system reliability, evidentiary integrity, and compliance with applicable legal and Department requirements.
Coordinating with the Customer Support Branch to establish service delivery and technical support expectations for BWC and digital evidence systems, including incident response, service request resolution, user access and account support, equipment troubleshooting, escalation procedures, system availability, and resolution of recurring technical issues.
Establishing service priorities and performance expectations for issues affecting sworn and civilian users and monitors support trends to identify systemic problems requiring corrective action, system enhancement, additional training, or escalation to vendors or other TSB technical components.
Coordinating with IT Infrastructure and Engineering, Desktop Support, Cybersecurity, Network Operations, application support personnel, MPD operational components, procurement and contracting personnel, vendors, and other technical stakeholders to plan and implement BWC and digital evidence system deployments, upgrades, integrations, maintenance activities, and operational improvements. Ensuring technical dependencies, security requirements, interoperability, resource requirements, schedules, and operational impacts are identified and addressed.
Collaborating with shareholders to plan for integration, improved operability, gather requirements, and maintain a high level of support for business operations. Developing, overseeing, and updating Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) governing BWC and digital evidence program operations to ensure consistent processes, accountability, regulatory compliance, and adherence to MPD policies and technical requirements.
Developing, reviewing, and updating Statements of Work (SOWs) for contracts and procurements supporting BWC and digital evidence systems, including system implementation, maintenance, technical support, upgrades, integrations, equipment, software, and professional services. Defining technical requirements, deliverables, performance standards, service-level expectations, timelines, and acceptance criteria to ensure contracted services meet MPD operational and program requirements.
Partnering with MPD operational commanders, investigative units, business owners, TSB leadership, technology managers, cybersecurity personnel, records and evidence stakeholders, legal and policy officials, and external technology partners to establish program requirements, priorities, implementation strategies, and service expectations for BWC and digital evidence systems. Facilitating resolution of competing operational and technical requirements and elevates significant risks, resource constraints, or policy issues to appropriate leadership for decision.
Developing and presenting program performance reports, dashboards, risk assessments, and executive briefings regarding BWC and digital evidence operations. Reporting on system performance, project milestones, vendor performance, service issues, budget status, compliance concerns, operational risks, and corrective actions to the DCIO, TSB leadership, and other authorized stakeholders.
Managing vendor and third-party relationships supporting BWC and digital evidence systems. Monitoring vendor performance against contractual requirements and service-level expectations; coordinating system maintenance, upgrades, technical support, and issue resolution; evaluating vendor recommendations; and escalatimg significant performance, security, contractual, or operational concerns through appropriate management and procurement channels. Leading the identification, analysis, documentation, and prioritization of business and technical requirements for BWC and digital evidence system enhancements, new functionality, integrations, and interfaces. Working with operational users, technical personnel, system owners, vendors, and other stakeholders to translate mission and business needs into defined system requirements and implementation priorities.
Planning and overseeing system testing, validation, and user acceptance activities for new BWC and digital evidence functionality, upgrades, integrations, and configuration changes. Ensuring appropriate technical personnel and business users verify system functionality, interoperability, security, performance, and operational readiness before production implementation. Overseeing training, documentation, change-management, and user-adoption activities associated with significant system changes.
Advising the Metropolitan Police Academy on the development and delivery of training related to assigned systems; and attending vendor-provided training. Developing and maintaining program procedures, business processes, internal controls, and governance practices necessary to support compliant BWC and digital evidence operations. Ensuring program activities align with applicable MPD policies, District requirements, records retention requirements, privacy requirements, cybersecurity controls, evidentiary standards, chain-of-custody requirements, and other applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
Leading and participating in technical and operational governance meetings concerning BWC and digital evidence system enhancements, integrations, configuration changes, service issues, and modernization initiatives. Evaluating proposed changes, identifying technical and operational impacts, coordinating stakeholder requirements, and developing recommendations regarding priorities and implementation.
Directing and overseeing processes governing the receipt, preservation, classification, retention, retrieval, redaction, authorized disclosure, transfer, and disposition of BWC and CCTV digital evidence within the program's responsibility. Establishing controls and quality assurance measures to protect evidentiary integrity, maintaining chain of custody, safeguarding sensitive information, and ensuring compliance with applicable records retention, privacy, disclosure, and evidentiary requirements.
Overseeing the establishment and maintenance of event classifications, metadata standards, retention schedules, access controls, and related digital evidence management configurations consistent with approved MPD policy and applicable legal requirements.
Establishing and maintaining BWC and digital evidence event-tagging classifications and associated retention requirements in coordination with MPD operational, legal, records management, and policy stakeholders. Ensuring event-tagging categories accurately reflect incident and evidentiary classifications and that associated retention periods comply with applicable MPD policies, District records-retention requirements, legal obligations, and evidentiary standards. Overseeing implementation of approved event-tagging and retention configurations within the digital evidence management system and evaluates proposed changes for operational, legal, and records-management impacts.
Overseeing the timely processing and fulfillment of authorized digital evidence requests from prosecutors, investigators, courts, public records functions, and other authorized entities. Ensuring appropriate controls are maintained for retrieval, review, redaction, disclosure, documentation, and transmission of digital evidence.
Serving as a technical subject-matter expert and, when required, provides testimony

Role Overview

The Digital Transformation (DT) Project Manager is responsible for the end-to-end delivery of MR DIY's digital and software initiatives spanning the mobile app, e-commerce, website, middleware, and supporting enterprise systems. The role plans, coordinates, and drives projects from initiation to closure, ensuring they are delivered on scope, on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards across multiple markets.

Working closely with product owners, engineering teams, vendors, and business stakeholders, the DT Project Manager translates business and technical requirements into structured delivery plans, manages dependencies and risks, and provides clear visibility of progress to leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Project Planning & Delivery
Develop and review business cases – lead the formulation and evaluation of comprehensive project business cases including ROI calculations and detailed costing to ensure financial alignment with strategic goals
Plan and drive delivery — build project plans, work breakdown structures, and schedules for digital/software implementation projects, from initiation through go-live and hypercare.
Manage scope, schedule, and budget — track progress against baseline, manage the change-control process for scope changes, and report cost and schedule variances.
Coordinate cross-functional delivery — align business analysts, developers, QA, vendors, and operations teams around a shared plan and shared milestones.

Testing & Quality Assurance
Apply testing-phase knowledge — understand unit, integration, system, regression, and UAT testing phases well enough to plan realistic test cycles and set clear exit criteria for each stage.
Partner with vendor and QA teams — work closely with vendor delivery teams and internal QA to make sure test coverage spans all angles — functional, integration, performance, security, and regression — not just the happy path.
Validate go-live readiness — review test results and defect burn-down against agreed exit criteria, and confirm sign-offs are in place before approving deployment.

Risk & Issue Management
Identify risks early — proactively surface technical, resourcing, vendor, and dependency risks during planning and throughout delivery, not just when they materialize.
Maintain a live risk register — log each risk with owner, likelihood, impact, and mitigation/contingency plan; review and update it on a regular cadence.
Track and escalate — monitor risk status through to closure, escalate material risks to sponsors and steering committees promptly, and report issue logs with root cause and resolution status.
Manage dependencies — map cross-project and cross-team dependencies and sequence delivery to avoid downstream schedule risk.

Project Checklists, Compliance & Governance
Maintain project checklists — work through structured stage-gate and go-live checklists covering compliance, security, data privacy, and operational readiness at each project milestone.
Uphold governance — ensure projects follow PMO standards, stage-gate approvals, and architectural, data, security, and compliance requirements before sign-off.

Change Management & Readiness
Coordinate change management — work with business owners, change management lead, and operations to build a change management plan covering communication, training, and support ahead of go-live.
Ensure training and SOP readiness — partner with relevant parties to confirm user training is delivered and SOPs are updated and in place so the organization is genuinely ready to adopt the new system, not just technically live.
Track benefits realization – Establish post-go-live monitoring to track benefits and KPIs, ensuring the solution achieves the outcomes defined in the original business case

Stakeholder & Vendor Management
Manage stakeholders — run steering committee updates, status reporting, and decision forums; keep sponsors informed with clear, honest status (green/amber/red) rather than optimistic reporting.

About WeRize

Founded in 2019 by Vishal Chopra and Himanshu Gupta, WeRize is building India’s largest full stack fintech platform for 500 million underserved middle-class customers who live in 5000+ small towns of India. WeRize (Wortgage technologies pvt ltd) also owns RBI registered NBFC subsidiary (Wortgage Finance pvt ltd).

This customer segments not served by private sector banks, Insurers and Mutual Fund companies due to their low ticket-size and lifetime value and is dependent on PSU/Govt. banks. PSU/Government banks rarely provide financial products beyond basic savings accounts and these customers lack access to unsecured loans, MSME loans, credit cards, affordable housing loans, loan against property , health and life insurance and investment products. WeRize manufactures innovative unsecured consumer credit, mortgages, loan against property, MSME loans, savings and insurance products designed for this customer base keeping in mind their needs, requirements and purchasing power, with a view to add a layer of financial security to their lives and enable access to credit. While customers in these geographies use smartphones, they need properguidance and support when purchasing the right financial products for themselves. So, a pure digital model doesn’t work for this segment. WeRize has innovated on this front through its ‘Finance ki online dukaan (Social Shopify of Finance)’, a first of its kind social distribution tech platform in the financial services space that educates and enables local financially literate freelancers across these small towns to source business through online and offline channels, recommend the right financial product(s) to customers as well as provide after sales support. These freelancers, who are located in more than 5000+ towns and cities, earn as much as INR 30,000 a month from WeRize in commissions.

Our social distribution platform supported by financially literate freelancers means exceptionally low cost of customer acquisition (CAC) and operations costs compared to both fully digital and on-the-ground financial services providers. Digital conversions among this target group are way lower when comparedto upper income customers in metros and hence pure digital CAC doesn’t workfor this segment. While companies like LIC and Fino Bank also rely on freelancer distribution, they deploy local on-field teams/branches to manage freelancers in every city. That results in very high CAC and operations costs for such companies. WeRize on the other hand, has been able to acquire, train and manage thousands of freelancers in 5000+ cities only through its tech platform and without any feet-on-street team of its own. This results in highly profitable business model for Werize.

Measure incremental conversion, repeat purchase, visit frequency, basket value, retention and reactivation. Assess contribution after reward and campaign costs, and recommend whether to scale, refine or stop a test.
Analyse customer segments, cohorts and purchase behaviour to identify growth opportunities. Monitor member acquisition, engagement, points and voucher redemption, lapsing and customer lifetime value where the available data supports reliable estimates.

Business intelligence and daily analytics

Extract, clean, validate and analyse sales, store, product, marketing and customer data. Investigate data quality issues and deliver accurate recurring reports and timely ad hoc analysis for management and business teams.

new_jobs.title: Youth Program Manager, Alpha - $200,000/year USD
new_jobs.description:
"the Great Educational Equalizer"

— Philosopher Johnathan Bi, on Alpha School

Alpha is hiring.

The best leaders don't measure success by what they accomplish themselves. They measure it by what the people around them achieve.

If you've run youth programs, built the staff and systems behind them, and hold people to a high bar while getting them to exceed it, this role offers the chance to apply those skills where they'll shape the next generation.

At Alpha, students don't spend their days listening to lectures. They master academics through adaptive technology while Guides focus on coaching, motivation, accountability, and life skills. As a Lead Guide, you'll build the team that makes this model work—coaching Guides, developing leaders, and creating an environment where students consistently exceed expectations.

This is not an instructional coaching role, and it is not classroom teaching. You won't spend your days reviewing lesson plans or observing lectures because there aren't any. Instead, you'll build a culture of excellence by coaching Guides, leading engaging life skills workshops, and motivating students to achieve ambitious goals. Your success will be measured by the quality of students' experiences, your team's performance, and your ability to maintain uncompromising standards while inspiring others to meet them.

Alpha is building the world's best K-12 experience. That requires leaders who have already proven they can raise others' performance, make objective, data-driven decisions, and embrace bold new ideas rather than protecting outdated traditions. If that describes you, we'd love to meet you.

This role is currently open at select Alpha campuses: Boston, MA; Raleigh, NC; New York City, NY; Greenwich, CT; and Washington, DC.

If you're located in one of these markets—or excited to relocate—we'd love to hear from you. Exceptional candidates outside these locations are also encouraged to apply. As Alpha continues to grow, we regularly match outstanding leaders with opportunities across our expanding network of campuses.

What You Will Be Doing

Coaching Guides to consistently deliver exceptional student experiences while maintaining Alpha's high standards.
Leading engaging life skills workshops that develop communication, leadership, focus, and other real-world skills for K-12 students.
Motivating students to achieve ambitious learning goals and maximize progress in their self-directed academic programs.
Using data, observation, and coaching conversations to improve Guide performance and student outcomes.
Helping launch and establish new Alpha campuses by building a culture centered on excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Teaching traditional academic classes or delivering subject-matter lectures.
Writing lesson plans or designing curriculum.
Lowering standards to make students feel successful instead of helping them achieve real mastery.
Managing a team from behind a desk without regularly coaching students and Guides firsthand.
Preserving outdated practices simply because "that's how we've always done it."

Youth Program Manager Key Responsibilities

Ensure every student consistently experiences Alpha's three promises by building high-performing Guides, delivering engaging life skills experiences, and maintaining uncompromising standards for student success.

Basic Requirements

Willingness to work on-site at an Alpha campus (relocation support available): Boston, MA; Raleigh, NC; New York City, NY; Greenwich, CT; Washington, DC
Bachelor's degree in Education, Psychology, Business, or a related field; Master's degree preferred.
At least 5 years of experience in education, coaching, learning and development, or a related leadership role.
Experience leading and developing teams of five or more people, including hiring and making performance-based termination decisions.
Demonstrated success using data to drive performance improvements.
Experience working with children ages 5-14 in an educational, coaching, or developmental setting.
Experience building or launching a new team, program, business, school, or initiative, with willingness to help open a new campus from zero.
Willingness to work in a school model that rejects traditional lecture-based pedagogy.
Legal authorization to work in the United States.

Nice-to-have Requirements

Experience coaching youth through athletics, debate, camps, or extracurricular programs.
Exceptional public speaking and storytelling skills.
A track record of achieving high levels of academic, professional, or athletic performance.
Experience motivating teams through ambitious goals while maintaining high accountability.
A passion for challenging conventional education and helping shape a new model for K-12 learning.

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

About Mind

Mind Robotics is building Physical AI for real-world industrial deployment, starting with the factory floor. We believe the hardest problems in AI are solved when researchers and engineers are hands-on with the physical world every day - and we're looking for people who are passionate about robotics, value ownership, and are excited to tackle difficult problems. Join us if you want to move beyond digital intelligence and put intelligence into motion.

About The Team And The Role

Program Management at Mind is an operational catalyst. We own outcomes, drive the trade-offs that keep engineering moving, and set the metabolic rate of the teams we partner with — clearing roadblocks, closing stalled decisions, carrying risk upward, and protecting the focus engineers need to build. As a Software Program Manager you will own the integrated program plan across all of software and build the practice itself: how teams define their own milestones and commit to org-level ones, how we know week over week whether we are on or off track, and how problems surface early enough that we can still do something about them. You will partner directly with hardware program management so that software and hardware roll up into one program picture rather than two competing ones.

Responsibilities

End-to-End Ownership: Own the software program plan end to end — from roadmap planning through implementation, integration, validation, and release to the fleet — and own the functional outcome, not just the schedule.
Program Practice Design: Establish how software program management works at Mind: the planning rhythm that connects team-level work to org-level milestones, what qualifies as a milestone, what "done" means at each one, and the artifacts that support both the individual engineer and leadership in prioritization and decision making.
Milestone Planning: Build software plans that align with org-level milestones, including clear definitions of what “done” means at each step.
Metric Tracking: Monitor and report on key program metrics, and communicate status, blockers, and risks to leadership.
Progress Tracking & Status Integrity: Build the tracking layer that answers whether we are on or off track, drawn from the systems teams already work in.
Risk Mitigation: Identify and escalate technical, dependency, and resourcing risks early, and and drive them to resolution.
Technical / Business Judgment: Engage directly in architecture and design discussions at a depth sufficient to stress-test engineering estimates and pressure-test readiness. Drive decisions at that level with understanding of the impacts to our business goals.

Requirements

Educational Background: Bachelor's degree in engineering (software / computer science preferred), or equivalent experience.
Industry Experience: 5+ years of experience in technical program management for software products, ideally in robotics, autonomous systems, or another domain where software ships against hardware and real-world deployment constraints.
Proven Track Record: Demonstrated success taking software from early development through release and sustained operation.
Technical Depth: Strong software fundamentals with the ability to engage meaningfully in architecture, planning, and systems integration discussions.
System Complexity: Experience managing programs spanning multiple interdependent software domains along with their dependencies on hardware revisions and the availability of test hardware.
Execution & Ownership: High sense of urgency, comfortable with ambiguity, and driven by an "engineering curiosity" to understand how the entire system works.

Job Description

Leverage your deep technical expertise and leadership to guide cutting-edge projects, fostering growth and innovation in a dynamic environment.

As a Lead Technical Program Manager at JPMorganChase within Infrastructure Platforms Foundational Services, you will drive the successful delivery of complex technology projects and programs that will help reaching business goals across the firm. Leveraging your deep knowledge of technical principles, practices, and theories is essential for developing innovative solutions, while simultaneously effectively managing resources, budgets, and high-performing teams. Your strong analytical reasoning and adaptability skills will enable you to navigate through ambiguity and change, ensuring that technology initiatives align with business goals. With advanced communication and stakeholder management abilities, you will foster productive working relationships and influence decision-making to achieve mutually beneficial outcomes. As a subject matter expert, you will contribute to the development of operational plans and risk management strategies, ensuring the highest quality and professionalism in service delivery.

Job responsibilities

Develop and execute comprehensive project plans, incorporating technical requirements, resource allocation, and timelines to ensure on-time delivery of technology solutions
Identify and mitigate risks, proactively addressing potential roadblocks and implementing contingency plans to maintain project and program momentum
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, product, and business stakeholders, to define program scope, objectives, and deliverables, ensuring alignment with overall business goals
Utilize advanced analytical reasoning to assess program performance, identify areas for improvement, and implement data-driven optimizations to enhance efficiency and effectiveness
Promotes reuse-first, AI-assisted practices for program governance and reporting, ensuring human review and alignment to delivery standards.
Champion the adoption of agile methodologies and technical solutions, fostering a culture of continuous learning and innovation within the team
Uses enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to accelerate program planning and risk synthesis (e.g., consolidating inputs into integrated plans, RAID, and executive-ready updates), validating outputs and handling data according to sensitivity requirements.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

5+ years of experience or equivalent expertise in technical program management, leading complex technology projects and programs in a large organization
Advanced expertise in stakeholder management, with the ability to establish productive working relationships and influence decision-making across cross-functional teams and clients
Advanced experience in utilizing technical fluency, including knowledge of vendor products and managing vendor relations, to enable on-demand access to shared pools of applications and services
Proven track record of effectively managing resources, budgets, and high-performing teams in a fast-paced, agile environment
Demonstrated proficiency in applying analytical reasoning and problem-solving techniques to break down business, technical, or operational objectives into manageable tasks and activities
Demonstrated experience using enterprise-authorized AI capabilities within the work environment to support program management workflows with strong validation habits and awareness of data sensitivity. (mandatory)
Ability to review and validate AI-assisted plans, risks, and recommendations before use, escalating when uncertain and following data handling expectations.
